first: चौ॰—प्रभु दोउ चाप-खंड महि डारे। देखि लोग सब भये सुखारे॥
en: The Lord threw the two pieces of the bow to the ground, and everyone who saw it was happy. Kaushika was like a holy ocean of beauty, full of the deep, lovely water of love;

first: राम रूप राकेस निहारी। बढ़त बीचि पुलकावलि भारी॥
en: looking at the full moon of Rama's beauty, great waves of thrills rose in it. Drums sounded loudly in the sky, and the wives of the gods danced and sang.

first: ब्रह्मादिक सुर सिद्ध मुनीसा। प्रभुहि प्रसंसहिँ देहिँं असीसा॥
en: Brahma and the other gods, the siddhas and the great sages praised the Lord and blessed him. They showered flowers and garlands of many colours, and the Kinnaras sang sweet songs.

first: रही भुवन भरि जय जय बानी। धनुष-भङ्ग धुनि जात न जानी॥
en: Cries of 'Victory, victory!' filled the worlds, so that the sound of the breaking bow could not be heard. Everywhere men and women said gladly, 'Rama has broken Shambhu's heavy bow.'

first: दो॰—बन्दी मागध सूत गन, बिरद बदहिँ मतिधीर।
en: Bards, minstrels and heralds, steady of mind, sang his praises, and all the people made offerings over him of horses, elephants, wealth, jewels and clothes.

first: चौ॰—झाँझ मृदङ्ग सङ्ख सहनाई। भेरि ढोल दुन्दुभी सुहाई॥
en: Cymbals, drums, conches, shehnais, kettledrums, drums and fine war drums, many lovely instruments, were played, and here and there young women sang songs of joy.

first: सखिन्ह सहित हरषीँ सब रानी। सूखत धान परा जनु पानी॥
en: All the queens and their friends were as glad as a drying rice crop when rain falls. Janaka felt joy, free of worry, like a tired swimmer who finds his footing.

first: श्रीहत भये भूप धनु टूटे। जैसे दिवस दीप छबि छूटे॥
en: The kings lost their glow when the bow broke, like lamps that lose their light by day. How can Sita's joy be told? It was like a chatak bird finding the water of the Swati star.

first: रामहिँ लखन बिलोकत कैसे। ससिहि चकोर किसारक जैसे॥
en: Lakshmana gazed at Rama like a young chakor bird at the moon. Then Shatananda gave the word, and Sita went towards Rama.

first: दो॰—सङ्ग सखी सुन्दर चतुर, गावहिँ मङ्गलचार।
en: With her went her lovely, clever friends singing songs of blessing. She moved with the gait of a young swan, her limbs full of endless grace.

first: चौ॰—सखिन्ह मध्य सिय सोहति कैसी। छबि-गन-मध्य महाछबि जैसी॥
en: How did Sita look among her friends? Like supreme beauty among many beauties. The lovely victory garland was in her lotus hand, shining with the glory of the conquest of the world.

first: तन सकोच मन परम उछाहू। गूढ़ प्रेम लखि परइ न काहू॥
en: Her body was shy, but her heart was full of eager joy; her deep love could not be seen by anyone. Going near and seeing Rama's beauty, the princess stood still like a painted picture.

first: चतुर सखी लखि कहा बुझाई। पहिरावहु जयमाल सुहाई॥
en: Seeing this, a clever friend urged her, 'Put the lovely victory garland on him.' Hearing this, she raised the garland with both hands, but she was so overcome by love that she could not put it on.

first: सोहत जनु जुग जलज सनाला। ससिहि सभीत देत जयमाला॥
en: Her raised hands looked like two lotuses with their stalks, timidly offering a victory garland to the moon. Seeing this beauty, her friends sang, and Sita placed the victory garland on Rama's neck.

first: सो॰—रघुबर उर जयमाल, देखि देव बरषहिँ सुमन॥
en: Seeing the victory garland on the chest of the best of the Raghus, the gods showered flowers. All the kings shrank back, like night lilies at the sight of the sun.

first: चौ॰—पुर अरु ब्योम बाजने बाजे। खल भये मलिन साधु सब राजे।
en: Music played in the city and in the sky; the wicked were downcast and all the good shone. Gods, Kinnaras, men, Nagas and great sages cried, 'Victory, victory, victory!' and gave their blessings.

first: नाचहिँ गावहिँ बिवुध-बधूटी। बार बार कुसुमाञ्जलि छूटी।
en: The wives of the gods danced and sang, and handfuls of flowers were showered again and again. Everywhere Brahmins chanted the Vedas, and heralds recited the praises of the family.

first: महि पाताल व्याल जस ब्यापा। राम बरी सिय भञ्जेउ चापा॥
en: The fame spread over earth, the lower worlds and heaven: Rama has broken the bow and won Sita. The men and women of the city waved lamps, and gave away gifts with no thought of their wealth.

first: सोहति सीय राम कै जोरी। छबि सिङ्गार मनहुँ इक ठोरी॥
en: The pair of Sita and Rama shone as if beauty and love had come together in one place. Her friends said, 'Sita, clasp the Lord's feet,' but she was too afraid to touch his feet.

first: दो॰—गौतम-तिय गति सुरति करि, नहिँ परसति पग पानि॥
en: Remembering what had happened to Gautama's wife, she would not touch his feet with her hands. The jewel of the Raghu line smiled inwardly, knowing her love was not of this world.

first: चौ॰—तब सिय देखि भूप अभिलाखे। कूर कपूत मूढ़ मन माखे॥
en: Then, seeing Sita, some kings were filled with desire; the cruel, unworthy and foolish among them grew angry. The wretches rose and put on armour, and began to boast here and there.

first: लेहु छड़ाइ सीय कह कोऊ। धरि बाँधहु नृप-बालक दोऊ॥
en: Some said, 'Snatch Sita away, and seize and tie up the two princes. Breaking the bow does not settle it; who can marry the princess while we are alive?'

first: जौँ बिदेह कछु करइ सहाई। जीतह समर सहित दोउ भाई॥
en: 'If Videha gives them any help, we will defeat him in battle along with the two brothers.' Hearing these words, the good kings spoke; even shame was ashamed of that gathering of kings.

first: बल प्रताप बीरता बड़ाई। नाक पिनाकहि सङ्ग सिधाई ॥
en: 'Your strength, glory, courage and honour went away along with the Pinaka bow. Is this the same valour, or have you found it somewhere now? With such thinking, the Creator has blackened your faces.'

first: दो०-देखहु रामहिँ नयन भरि, तजि इरषा मद कोहु ।
en: 'Look at Rama with full eyes and give up envy, pride and anger. Know that Lakshmana's anger is a mighty fire, and do not become moths.'

first: चौ०--वैनतेय बलि जिमि चह कागू । जिमि सस चहइ नाग-अरिभागू।
en: 'It is like a crow wanting Garuda's share, a hare wanting a lion's share, one angry without cause wanting peace, or an enemy of Shiva wanting every kind of wealth;'

first: लोभी लोलुप कीरति'चहई ।अकलङ्कता कि कामी लहई ।
en: 'like a greedy man wanting fame, a lustful man wanting a spotless name, or one turned from Hari's feet wanting salvation: such is your longing, kings.'

first: कोलाहल सुनि सीय सकानी । सखी लेवाइ गई जहँ रानी,॥
en: Hearing the uproar, Sita grew anxious, and her friends took her to where the queens were. Rama went calmly to the guru, praising Sita's love in his heart.

first: रानिन्ह सहित सोच बस सीयो । अब धौँ बिधिहि काह करनीया ॥
en: Sita and the queens were worried: 'What will fate do now?' Hearing the kings' words, Lakshmana looked this way and that, but in awe of Rama he could not speak.

first: दो०--अरुन-नयन भृकुटी-कुटिल, चितवत नृपन्ह सकोप ।
en: With red eyes and bent brows he glared angrily at the kings, like a young lion eager to pounce on seeing a herd of maddened elephants.

first: चौ०--खरसर देखि विकल पुर-नारी । सबमिलि देहि महीपन्ह गारो॥
en: Seeing the commotion, the women of the city were upset and all together cursed the kings. Just then, hearing of the breaking of Shiva's bow, Parashurama came, the sun to the lotus of the Bhrigu clan.

first: देखि महीप सकल सकुचाने । बाज झपट जनु लवा लुकाने ॥
en: Seeing him, all the kings shrank back, like quails hiding from the swoop of a hawk. His fair body shone with ash, and the three lines of Shiva's mark shone on his broad forehead.

first: सोस-जदा सास-बदन सुहावा । रिस-बस कछुक अरुन होइ आवा ।
en: Matted hair on his head, his lovely moon-like face had turned somewhat red with anger. His brows were bent and his eyes red with rage, so that even his normal look seemed angry.

first: वृषभ कन्ध उर-बाहु बिलासा । चारु जनेउ मोल मृगछाला ॥
en: He had a bull's shoulders and a broad chest and arms, a fine sacred thread, a rosary and a deerskin. At his waist was a hermit's cloth with two quivers tied on, a bow and arrows in his hands and a fine axe on his shoulder.

first: दो०--सान्त बेष करनी कठिन, बरनि न जाइ सरूप ।
en: A peaceful dress but harsh deeds, a form beyond words: it was as if the heroic mood itself, in a sage's body, had come to where the kings were.

first: चौ०-देखत भूगुपति मेष कराला । उठे सकल भय-विकल भुआला ॥
en: Seeing Parashurama's fearsome form, all the kings rose, shaking with fear. Each told his own name and his father's, and fell flat in salutation.

first: जेहि सुभाय चितवहिँ हित जानी । सो जानड़ जनु आयु खुटानी ॥
en: Even the one he looked at kindly felt that his life had come to an end. Then Janaka came and bowed his head, and called Sita to bow to him.

first: आसिष दीन्हि सखी हरषानी । निज समाज लइ गईं सयानी ॥
en: He gave her his blessing, and her friends, glad, wisely took her back to her group. Then Vishvamitra came and met him, and placed the two brothers at his lotus feet.

first: राम लखन दसरथ के ढोटा। दीन्हि असीस देखि भल जोटा ।
en: 'Rama and Lakshmana, sons of Dasharatha.' Seeing the fine pair, he blessed them. His eyes rested on Rama, whose endless beauty took away the pride of Love.

first: दो०--बहुरि बिलोकि बिदेह सन, कहहु काह अति भीर ।
en: Then he looked at Videha and asked, 'Tell me, why is there such a crowd?' He asked as if he did not know, though he did, and anger spread through his body.

first: चौ०-समाचार कहि जनक सुनाये । जेहि कारन महीप सब आये ॥
en: Janaka told him the news and the reason all the kings had come. Hearing this, he turned and looked the other way and saw the pieces of the bow lying on the ground.

first: अति रिस बोलें बचन कठोरा । कहु जड़ जनक धनुष केइ तोरा ।
en: In great anger he spoke harsh words: 'Tell me, foolish Janaka, who broke the bow? Show him to me quickly, fool, or today I will overturn the earth as far as your kingdom reaches.'

first: अति डर उतर देत नृप नाहीं। कुटिल भूप हरषे मन माहीं ।
en: In great fear the king gave no answer, and the crooked kings were glad at heart. Gods, sages, Nagas and the men and women of the city all grieved, with great fear in their hearts.

first: मन पछिताति सीय-महँतारी। बिधि अब सबरी बात बिगारी॥
en: Sita's mother lamented in her heart: 'The Creator has now spoiled everything.' Hearing of Parashurama's nature, half a moment felt to Sita like an age.

first: दो०--समय बिलोके लोग सब, जानि जानकी भीर।
en: Rama looked at all the people and, knowing Janaki's fear, the glorious hero of the Raghus spoke, with neither joy nor sorrow in his heart.

first: चौ०--नाथ सम्भु-धनु भञ्जनिहारा । होइहि कोउ एक दास तुम्हारा ॥
en: 'Master, the one who broke Shambhu's bow must be some servant of yours. What is your order? Why not tell me?' Hearing this, the angry sage spoke in a rage.

first: सेवक सो जो करई सेवकाई । अरि करनी करि करिय लराई ।
en: 'A servant is one who does service; one who acts like an enemy must be fought. Listen, Rama, whoever broke Shiva's bow is my enemy, like the thousand-armed Sahasrabahu.'

first: सो बिलगाउ बिहाइ समाजा। नत मारे जइहैं सब राजा ॥
en: 'Let him stand apart from this crowd, or all the kings will be killed.' Hearing the sage's words, Lakshmana smiled and spoke to the axe-bearer mockingly.

first: बहु धनुही तोरी लरकाँई । कबहुँ न असि रिस कीन्हि गुसाँई ॥
en: 'In our childhood we broke many little bows, and you never got so angry, master. Why such attachment to this bow?' Hearing this, the banner of the Bhrigu clan said angrily,

first: दो०--रे नृप-बालक काल-बस, बोलत तोहि न सँभार।
en: 'You prince in the grip of Death, you do not watch your words! Is the bow of Shiva, the enemy of the three cities, famous through the whole world, like a little toy bow?'

first: चौ०--लखन कहा हाँसि हमरे जाना । सुनहु देव सब धनुष समाना ॥
en: Lakshmana laughed and said, 'Listen, lord, to us all bows are the same. What loss or gain is there in breaking an old bow? Rama took it for a new one,'

first: छुअत टूट रघुपतिहु न दोषू । मुनि बिनु काज करिय कत रोषु ।
en: 'and it broke at his touch; the Lord of the Raghus is not to blame. Sage, why be angry for nothing?' Looking at his axe, Parashurama said, 'Fool, have you not heard of my nature?'

first: बालक बोलि बघउँ नहिँ तोही । केवल मुनि जड़ जानहि मोही।
en: 'I do not kill you, thinking you a child; you, fool, take me for a mere sage. I have been celibate from childhood, very wrathful, and known to the world as the enemy of the warrior clans.'

first: भुज-बल भूमि भूप बिनु कीन्ही । बिपुल बार महिंदेवन्ह दोन्ही ॥
en: 'By the strength of my arms I made the earth empty of kings and gave it many times to the Brahmins. Prince, look at this axe that cut off the arms of the thousand-armed one.'

first: दो०--मातु-पितहि जनि सोच बस, करसि महीप-किसोर।
en: 'Prince, do not make your mother and father grieve. My axe is so terrible that it destroys even unborn babies in the womb.'

first: चौ०--बिहँसि लखन बोले मृदुबानी । अहो मुनीस महा अट मानी॥
en: Lakshmana smiled and said softly, 'Oh, great sage, what a proud warrior you are! Again and again you show me your axe, as if you wanted to blow away a mountain with a puff.'

first: इहाँ कुम्हड़-बतिया कोउ नाहीं । जे तरजनी देखि मरि जाहीं ॥
en: 'There are no tiny gourd buds here that wilt at the sight of a pointing finger. It was seeing your axe, bow and arrows that I spoke a little proudly.'

first: भृगुकुल समुझि जनेउ बिलोकी । जो कछु कहहु सहउँ रिस रोकी ॥
en: 'Knowing you to be of the Bhrigu clan and seeing your sacred thread, I hold back my anger and bear whatever you say. In our family we show no valour against gods, Brahmins, devotees of Hari and cows.'

first: बधे पाप अपकीरति हारे । भारतहूँ पाँ परिय तुम्हारे ।
en: 'Killing them brings sin, and losing to them brings shame; so even if you strike us, we must fall at your feet. Your words alone are like ten million thunderbolts; you carry bow, arrows and axe for nothing.'

first: दो०--जो बिलोकि अनुचित कहेउँ, छमहु महा मुनि धीर ।
en: 'Great and steady sage, forgive whatever improper thing I said on seeing these.' Hearing this, the jewel of the Bhrigu line spoke angrily in a deep voice.

first: चौ०--कौसिक सुनहु मन्द यह बालक । कुटिल काल बस निज कुल घालक॥
en: 'Kaushika, listen, this boy is dull, crooked and in the grip of Death, a ruin to his own family. He is a stain on the moon of the Sun dynasty, wholly unruly, foolish and fearless.'

first: काल-कवलु होइहि छन माहीं । कहउँ पुकारि खोरि माहि नाहीं
en: 'In a moment he will be a mouthful for Death; I warn you loudly, and the blame will not be mine. If you want to save him, stop him by telling him of my glory, strength and anger.'

first: लखन कहेउ मुनि सुजस तुम्हारा । तुम्हहिँ अछत्त को बरनइ पारा ॥
en: Lakshmana said, 'Sage, while you are here, who else could describe your fame? With your own mouth you have told of your own deeds many times, in many ways.'

first: दो--सूर समर करनी करहिँ, कहि न जनावहिँ आप ।
en: 'Heroes do great deeds in battle and do not boast about them. Cowards, finding an enemy before them in battle, just babble.'

first: चौ०--तुम्ह तौ काल हाँक जनु लावा। बार बार मोहि लागि घुलावा॥
en: 'You seem to be calling Death to me, and you call him again and again for my sake.' Hearing Lakshmana's harsh words, Parashurama gripped his terrible axe firmly in his hand.

first: अब जनि देइं दोष माहि लोगू ।कटुबादी बालक बध जोगू ॥
en: 'Now let no one blame me; this harsh-tongued boy deserves to die. Seeing he was a child, I spared him a lot, but now he is truly about to die.'

first: कौसिक कहा छमिय अपराधू । बाल दोष-गुन गनहिँ न साधू ॥
en: Kaushika said, 'Forgive his fault; good people do not count a child's faults and merits.' 'Axe in hand, I am angry without mercy, and before me stands a sinner against my guru.'

first: उत्तर देत छाड़उँ बिनु मारे। केवल 'कासिक सील तुम्हारे ॥
en: 'Only for your goodness, Kaushika, do I let him go without killing him, though he answers back. Otherwise, with this harsh axe, I would easily have repaid my debt to my guru.'

first: दो०--गाधि-सूनु कह हृदय हँसि, मुनिहि हरिअरइ सूत्र ।
en: The son of Gadhi laughed in his heart: 'The sage sees only green everywhere. This is a sword of steel, not of sugarcane; yet the fool does not understand.'

first: चौ०--कहेउ लखन मुनि सील तुम्हारा । को नहिं जान बिदित संसारा॥
en: Lakshmana said, 'Sage, who does not know your goodness? It is famous in the world. You have fully paid your debt to your mother and father; only the debt to your guru is left, and that weighs on your heart.'

first: सो जनु हमरेहि माथे काढ़ा । दिन चलि गयउ व्याज बहु बाढ़ा।
en: 'It seems you have taken that on our account. Much time has passed, and the interest has grown a lot. Now call the money-lender, and I will at once open my purse and pay.'

first: सुनि कटु-बचन कुठार सुधारा । हाय हाय सब सभा पुकारा ।
en: Hearing these bitter words, he raised his axe, and the whole assembly cried, 'Alas, alas!' Lakshmana said, 'Best of the Bhrigus, you show me your axe, but, enemy of kings, I spare you because you are a Brahmin.'

first: मिले न कबहुँ ,सुभट रन गाढ़े। द्विज-देवता घरहिँ के बोढ़े।
en: 'You have never met strong warriors in hard battle; Brahmin god, you have grown big only at home.' Everyone cried, 'This is wrong!' and the Lord of the Raghus checked Lakshmana with a sign.

first: दो०--लखन उतर आहुति सरिस, भृगुषर कोप कृसानु ।
en: Seeing Parashurama's anger blaze up like a fire fed by the offerings of Lakshmana's replies, the sun of the Raghu clan spoke words cool as water.

first: चौ०--नाथ करहु बालक पर छोहू । सूध दूध-मुख करिय न कोहू
en: 'Master, be kind to the boy; do not be angry with an innocent child still smelling of milk. If he knew anything of your power, would he, so ignorant, try to match you?'

first: जौँ लरिका कछु अचगरि करहाँ । गुरु पितु मातु माद मन अरहीं।
en: 'If a child is a little naughty, his guru, father and mother are glad at heart. Know him as a child and a servant and be kind to him; you are a sage, good, patient and wise.'

first: राम बचन सुनि कछुक जुड़ाने । कहि कछु लखन बहुरि मुसुकाने ॥
en: Hearing Rama's words he cooled a little, but Lakshmana said something more and smiled again. Seeing him laugh, anger spread through him from head to toe: 'Rama, your brother is very wicked.'

first: गौर शरीर स्याम मन माहीं। कालकूट -मुख पय-मुख नाहीं ॥
en: 'Fair of body but dark of mind; he has poison in his mouth, not milk. Crooked by nature, he does not follow you; the wretch does not see me as Death.'

first: दो०--लखन कहेउ हँसि सुनहु मुनि, क्रोध पाप कर मूल ।
en: Lakshmana laughed and said, 'Listen, sage, anger is the root of sin. Under its power people do wrong and set themselves against the world.'

first: चौ०--मैं तुम्हार अनुचर मुनिराया। परिहरि कोप करिय अब दाया॥
en: 'King of sages, I am your servant; give up anger and show mercy now. The broken bow will not join through anger. Please sit; your feet must be aching from standing.'

first: जौँ अति प्रिय ती करिय उपाई। जोरिय कोउ बड़ गुनी बालाई ॥
en: 'If you love the bow so much, find a way: call some great craftsman and have it joined.' As Lakshmana spoke, Janaka was afraid: 'Be quiet; speaking wrongly is not good.'

first: थर थर कापहिँ पुर-नर-नारी । छोट कुमार खोट अति मारी ।
en: The men and women of the city trembled: 'The little prince is very naughty.' Hearing again and again his fearless words, Parashurama's body burned with rage and his strength drained away.

first: बोले रामहि देइ निहोरा । बचउँ बिचारि बन्धु लघु तारा ॥
en: He spoke to Rama as a favour: 'I spare your little brother only out of regard for you. Dirty of mind but lovely of body, he is like a golden pot full of poison.'

first: दो०--सुनि लछिमन बिहँ से बहुरि, नैन तरेरे राम ।
en: Hearing this, Lakshmana laughed again, and Rama gave him a stern look. Lakshmana shyly went to the guru, giving up his harsh words.

first: चौ०--अति बिनीत मृदु सीतल बानी। बोले राम जोरि जुग पानी॥
en: Joining both hands, Rama spoke very humbly in soft, cool words: 'Listen, master, you are wise by nature; do not take a child's words to heart.'

first: बररे बालक एक सुभाऊ । इन्हहिँ न बिदुष बिदूषहिँ काऊ ॥
en: 'Wasps and children are alike by nature; the wise never blame them. He has done no harm at all; master, I am the one at fault.'

first: कृपा कोप बध बन्ध गोसाँई । मो पर करिय दास की नाँई ।
en: 'Master, show me kindness or anger, kill me or bind me, as you would a servant. Tell me quickly how your anger may go, chief of sages, and I will do it.'

first: कह मुनि राम जाइ रिस कैसे। अजहुँ अनुज तव चितव अनैसे॥
en: The sage said, 'Rama, how can my anger go? Even now your brother looks at me rudely. If I did not bring my axe down on his neck, then I have been angry for nothing.'

first: दो०--गर्भ सवहिँ अवनिप-रवनि, सुनि कुठार-गति-घोर।
en: 'The wives of kings miscarried on hearing of my terrible axe; yet with the axe in my hand I see this enemy prince alive.'

first: चौ०--बहइ न हाथ दहइ रिस छाती। मा कुठार कुठित प-घाती।
en: 'My hand will not strike, yet anger burns my chest; my axe, killer of kings, has become blunt. Fate has turned against me and my nature has changed; how did pity ever come into my heart?'

first: आजु दया दुख दुसह सहावा । सुनि सौमित्रि विहँसि सिर नावा।
en: 'Today pity has made me bear unbearable pain.' Hearing this, Sumitra's son smiled and bowed his head: 'Your gust of kindness suits your form; your words fall like flowers.'

first: जौँ पै कृपा जरहिँ मुनि गाता । क्रोध भये तनु राखु विधाता ॥
en: 'If your body burns with kindness, sage, then when you are angry, may God protect your body!' 'Look, Janaka, this foolish boy is set on making his home in the city of Death.'

first: बेगि करहु किन आँखिन्ह ओटा। देखत छोट खोट नृप ढाटा ॥
en: 'Why not quickly take him out of my sight? He looks small, but the prince is very wicked.' Lakshmana laughed and said to himself, 'Close your eyes, and no one is anywhere.'

first: दो०--परसुराम तब राम प्रति, बोले उर अति क्रोध ।
en: Then Parashurama spoke to Rama with great anger in his heart: 'Wretch, you broke Shambhu's bow, and now you try to teach me?'

first: चौ०--बन्धु कहइ कटु सम्मत तेरे । तू छल बिनय करसि कर जारे ।
en: 'Your brother speaks bitterly with your consent, and you plead falsely with joined hands. Satisfy me in battle, or stop calling yourself Rama.'

first: छल तजि करहि समर सिव-द्रोही । बन्धु सहित न त मारउँ ताही ।
en: 'Enemy of Shiva, give up deceit and fight me, or I will kill you along with your brother.' Parashurama ranted with his axe raised, while Rama bowed his head and smiled inwardly.

first: गुनहु लखन कर हम पर रोषू । कतहुँ सुधाइहु तँ बड़ दोषू ।
en: 'Lakshmana is at fault, but you are angry with me; sometimes even gentleness is a great fault. Everyone fears what is crooked; Rahu does not swallow the crescent moon.'

first: राम कहेउ रिस तजिय मुनीसा । कर कुठार आगे यह सीसा ॥
en: Rama said, 'Give up anger, chief of sages; your axe is in your hand and here is my head. Master, do whatever will quench your anger; know me as your follower.'

first: दो०--प्रभुहि सेवकहि समर कस, तजहु विप्र-बर रोस ।
en: 'How can there be a fight between master and servant? Best of Brahmins, give up anger. The boy said something on seeing your warrior's dress; even he is not to blame.'

first: चौ०--देखि कुठार बान-धनु-धारी । भइ लरिकहि रिस बीर बिचारी॥
en: 'Seeing you with axe, arrows and bow, the boy took you for a warrior and got angry. He knew your name but did not recognise you, and answered as is the nature of his family.'

first: जौँ तुम्ह अवतेहु मुनि की नाँई । पद-रज सिर सिसु धरत गोसाँई।
en: 'If you had come as a sage, master, the child would have put the dust of your feet on his head. Forgive the mistake of one who did not know; a Brahmin's heart should be full of kindness.'

first: हमाहिँ तुम्हहिँ सरबरि कस नाथा । कहहु न कहाँ चरन कहँ माथा ॥
en: 'How can we be your equal, master? Tell me, where are the feet and where the head? My name is just short "Rama", while yours is great, joined with the axe.'

first: देव एक गुन धनुष हमारे । नव गुन परम-पुनीत तुम्हारे ।
en: 'Lord, my bow has one string, while yours are nine most holy virtues. In every way we are beaten by you; Brahmin, forgive our fault.'

first: दो०--बार बार मुनि बिप्र घर, कहा राम सन राम !
en: Again and again Rama called Parashurama 'sage' and 'Brahmin'. The lord of the Bhrigus laughed angrily: 'You are as crooked as your brother.'

first: चौ०--निपटहि द्विज करिजानहिमाही। मैं जस बिप्र सुनावउँ तोही ॥
en: 'You take me for a mere Brahmin; let me tell you what kind of Brahmin I am. Know my bow as the sacrificial ladle, my arrows as the offerings, and my anger as the terrible fire;'

first: समिध सेन चतुरङ्ग सुहाई । महा-महीप भये पसु आई ॥
en: 'the fine four-part armies as the fuel; great kings came as the animals of sacrifice. With this axe I cut them up as offerings, and I have done ten million sacrifices of war in this world.'

first: मोर प्रभाव विदित नहिँ तोरे । बोलसि निदरि बिन के भोरे ॥
en: 'You do not know my power; you speak with scorn, taking me for a mere Brahmin. Having broken the bow, your pride has grown great, as if your ego stood there having conquered the world.'

first: राम कहा मुनि कहहु विचारो। रिस अति बडि लघु चूक हमारी।
en: Rama said, 'Sage, speak with thought. Your anger is very great and my mistake very small. The old Pinaka broke at a touch; why should I be proud?'

first: दो०--जौँ हम निदरहिं विप्र बदि, सत्य सुनहु भृगुनाथ ।
en: 'Lord of the Bhrigus, hear the truth: if, as you say, we look down on you as a Brahmin, then who is the warrior in the world before whom we would bow our heads in fear?'

first: चौ०--देव दनुज भूपति अट नाना । सम बल अधिक होउ बलवाना ।
en: 'Gods, demons, kings and many warriors, whether equal to us in strength or stronger: if any of them challenges us to battle, we will gladly fight him, even if he is Death himself.'

first: छत्रिय धरि समर सकाना । कुल-कलङ्क तेहि पावर जाना ॥ कहउँ सुभाव न कुलहि प्रसंसी । कालहु डरहिन रन रघुवंसी ॥२॥
en: 'One born a warrior who, in battle, fears for his life is a stain on his family and a wretch. I speak by nature, not to praise my family: the Raghus do not fear even Death in battle.'

first: बिप्र-बस के असि प्रभुताई । अभय हाइ जो तुम्हहिं डेराई ॥ सुनि मृदु गूढ़ बचन रघुपति के । उघरे पटल परसुधर-मति के ॥३॥
en: 'Such is the greatness of the Brahmin race that one who fears you becomes free of all fear.' Hearing the gentle, deep words of the Lord of the Raghus, the veil over the axe-bearer's mind was lifted.

first: राम रमापति कर धनु लेहू । खैचहु मार मिटै सन्देहू ॥ देत चाप आपुहि चलि गयऊ । परसुराम मन बिसमय भयऊ॥
en: 'Rama, take this bow of Vishnu, Lakshmi's lord, and draw it, so that my doubt may end.' As he offered it, the bow went to Rama of its own accord, and Parashurama was amazed.

first: दो-जाना राम प्रभाव तब, पुलक प्रफुल्लित गात ॥ जोरि पानि बोले बचन, हृदय न प्रेम अमात ॥२८॥
en: Then he knew Rama's power, and his body thrilled and glowed. Joining his hands, he spoke, his heart unable to hold its love.

first: चौ०-जय रघुबंस-बनज-बन-मोनू । गहन-दनुज-कुल दहन-कसानू ॥ जय सुर-बिन-धेनु-हितकारी । जय मद मोह-कोह-मभ-हारी ॥१॥
en: 'Glory to you, sun to the lotus grove of the Raghu clan, fire to the dense forest of demons! Glory to you, friend of gods, Brahmins and cows! Glory to you, destroyer of pride, delusion, anger and fear!'

first: बिनय-सील करुना-गुन सागर । जयति बचन-रचना अति नागर ॥ सेवक-सुखद सुभग सब अङ्गा । जय सरीर छबि कोटि अनङ्गा ॥२॥
en: 'Ocean of humility, goodness, mercy and virtue, glory to you, master of graceful speech! Giver of joy to your servants, lovely in every limb, glory to you, whose body has the beauty of millions of Love gods!'

first: करउँ काह मुख एक प्रसंसा । जय महेस मन मानस हंसा ॥ अनुचित बहुत कहेउँ अज्ञाता । छम छमा मन्दिर दोउ माता ॥३॥
en: 'How can I praise you with one mouth? Glory to you, swan in the lake of Mahesh's mind! I said many wrong things in ignorance; forgive me, both of you brothers, homes of forgiveness.'

first: कहि जय जय जय रघुकुलकेतू । भृगुपति गये बनहिँ तप-हेतू ॥ अपभय कुटिल महीप डेराने । जहँ तह कायर गँवहिं पराने ॥४॥
en: Saying 'Victory, victory, victory to the banner of the Raghu clan!', Parashurama went to the forest for penance. The crooked kings grew afraid without cause, and the cowards slipped away here and there.

first: देवन्ह दीन्ही दुन्दभी, प्रभु पर बरषहिँ फूल॥ हर पुर-नर-नारि सब, मिटा मोह-मय-सूल ॥२८॥
en: The gods beat their drums and showered flowers on the Lord. All the men and women of the city were glad; the pain of their delusion and fear was gone.

first: चौ-अति गहगहे बाजने बाजे। सहि मनोहर मङ्गल साजे ॥ जूथ जूथ मिलि सुमुखि सुनयनी । करहिं गान कल कोकिल-बयनी ॥१॥
en: Music played loudly, and lovely, auspicious things were arranged. Groups of lovely-faced, bright-eyed women with voices like cuckoos sang sweetly.

first: सुख बिदेह कर बरनि न जाई । जनम दरिद्र मनहुँ निधि पाई ॥ बिगत नास भइ पीय सुखारी । जनु बिधु उदय चकोर-कुमारी ॥२॥
en: Videha's joy cannot be told; it was as if a man poor from birth had found a treasure. Freed from fear, Sita was happy, like a young chakor bird when the moon rises.

first: जनक कीन्ह कैासिकहि मनोमा । प्रभु प्रसाद धनु भउजेउ रामा ॥ मोहि कृतकृत्य कीन्ह दुहुँ भाई । अब जोउचित सो कहिय गोसाँई ॥३॥
en: Janaka bowed to Kaushika: 'By your grace, master, Rama has broken the bow. The two brothers have fulfilled my life; now, master, tell me what is right to do.'

first: कह मुनि सुनु नरनाथ प्रवीना । रहा विवाह चाप आधीना ॥ दूटत ही धनु भयेउ बिवाहू । सुर नर नाग विदित सब काहू ॥४॥
en: The sage said, 'Listen, wise king, the marriage depended on the bow; as soon as it broke, the marriage was settled, as gods, men and Nagas all know.'

first: दो-तदपि जाइ तुम्ह करहु अब,जथा वंस व्यवहार ॥ बूझि विप्र कुल-बुद्ध गुरु, बेइ विदित आचार ॥२६॥
en: 'Even so, go now and do what the customs of your family require, asking the Brahmins, the elders of your clan and your guru, for they know the proper ways.'

first: दो-दूत अवधपुर पठवहु जाई । आनहिँ नप दसरथहि बोलाई ॥ मुदित राउ कहि भलेहि कृपाला । पठये दूत बालि तेहि काला ॥१॥
en: 'Send messengers to Ayodhya to invite King Dasharatha and bring him here.' The king gladly said, 'Very well, kind one,' and at once called messengers and sent them.

first: बहुरि महाजन सकल बोलाये। आइ सबन्हि सादर सिर नाये ॥ हाट बार मन्दिर सुर-बासा । नगर सँवारहु चारिहु पासा ॥२॥
en: Then he called all the leading citizens; they came and respectfully bowed their heads. 'Decorate the markets, streets, houses and temples, and the whole city on all four sides.'

first: हरषि चले निज निज गृह आये। पुनि परिचारक बालि पठाये ॥ रचहु बिचित्र बितान बनाई। सिर धरि बचन चले सचु पाई ॥३॥
en: They went home gladly. Then the king called his servants and sent them: 'Make a wonderful wedding canopy.' They took his order on their heads and went happily.

first: पठये बालि गुनी तिन्ह नाना । जे मितान विधि कुसल सुजाना ॥ बिधिहि बन्दि तिन्ह कीन्ह अरम्माविरचे कनक कदलि के खम्मा॥
en: They called many craftsmen who were skilled and wise in making canopies. Bowing to Brahma, they began work and made pillars shaped like banana trees of gold.

first: दो०-हरित-मनिन्ह के. पन्न फल, पदुमराग के फूल ॥ रचना देखि बिचित्र अति, मन बिच्चि कर भूल ॥२८॥
en: With leaves and fruit of green emerald and flowers of ruby, the work was so wonderful that even the Creator was confused on seeing it.

first: चौ०-बेनु हरित-मनि-मय सब कीन्हे। सरल सुपरन परहिँ नहिं चोन्है ॥ कनक कलित अहिबेलि बनाई। लखि नहिं परइ सपरन सुहाई ॥१॥
en: All the bamboo poles were made of green gems, so straight and with such fine joints that they could not be told from real. Betel vines of gold were made, so lovely with their leaves that they could not be told apart.

first: तेहि के रचि पचि बन्ध बनाये ॥ बिच बिच मुकुता-दाम लगाये मानिक मरकत कुलिस पिरोजा। चोरि कोरि पचि रचे सरोजा ॥२॥
en: These were carefully worked into bands, with strings of pearls set here and there. Rubies, emeralds, diamonds and turquoise were cut, carved and set to make lotuses.

first: किये भृङ्ग बहुरि बिहङ्गा। गुजहिँ कूहिँ पवन प्रसङ्गा॥
en: Bees and many kinds of birds were made, which hummed and sang when the wind blew. Images of gods were carved on the pillars, all standing with auspicious things in their hands.

first: चौ भाँति अनेक पुराई। सिन्धुर-मनि मय सहज सुहाई॥४॥
en: Squares were filled with many kinds of designs, made with elephant pearls and naturally lovely.

first: दो॰ – सौरम-पल्लव सुभग सुठि, किये नीलमनि कोरि।।
en: Very lovely mango leaves were carved from sapphires, and mango blossoms of gold with emerald stems shone on silk cords.

first: चौ॰ – रुचिर बर बन्दनवारे। मनहुँ मनोभव फन्द सँवारे॥
en: Fine, lovely festoons were made, as if Love had set his snares. Many auspicious water pots were made, with flags, banners, cloth and fine whisks.

first: दीप मनोहर मनि-मय नाना। जाइ अरनि विचित्र बिताना॥
en: There were many charming lamps made of gems; the wonderful canopy cannot be described. Who has the mind to describe the pavilion in which Vaidehi is the bride?

first: दूलह राम रूप-गुन-सागर। सो वितान तिहुँ लोक उजागर॥
en: The bridegroom was Rama, an ocean of beauty and virtue, so that canopy shone through the three worlds. The beauty of Janaka's palace could be seen in every house in the city.

first: जेहि तिरहुति तेहि समय निहारी। तेहि लघु लोग भुवन दस-चारी॥
en: Whoever saw Tirhut at that time thought the fourteen worlds small. The wealth that shone in even a humble house charmed the king of the gods himself.

first: दो॰ – बसइ नगरजेहि लच्छि करि, कपट नारि बर बेष।
en: How can one tell the beauty of the city where Lakshmi herself lived in disguise as a fine woman? Even Sharada and Shesha shrink from describing it.

first: चौ॰ – पहुँचे दूत राम-पुर पावन। हरष नगर बिलोकि सुहावन।
en: The messengers reached Rama's holy city and were glad to see its beauty. They sent word at the king's gate, and King Dasharatha heard and called them in.

first: करि प्रनाम तिन्ह पाती दोन्ही। मुदित महीप आप उठि लीन्ही॥
en: They bowed and handed over the letter, and the king gladly rose and took it himself. Reading it, his eyes filled with tears, his body thrilled and his chest swelled.

first: राम-लखन-उर कर-नर-चीठी। रहि गये कहत न खाटी मीठी॥
en: With Rama and Lakshmana in his heart and the letter in his hand, he could not say whether it was bitter or sweet. Then, taking courage, he read the letter aloud, and the court rejoiced to hear the true news.

first: खेलत रहे तहाँ सुधि पाई। आये भरत सहित हित भाई॥
en: Bharata, who was playing nearby, heard the news and came with his friends and brother. With great love, but shyly, he asked, 'Father, where has the letter come from?'

first: दो॰ – कुसल प्रान प्रिय बन्धु दोउ, अहहिँ कहहु केहि देस।
en: 'Are my two brothers, dear as life, well? Tell me, in which land are they?' Hearing these words full of love, the king read the letter again.
